(c) Apply uniform_of_equilipschitz with K = closedBall 0 R (isCompact_closedBall), F k x = ∫ y in ball 0 (2R), u k y * φ (x − y), a = c * ∫ φ and Lipschitz constant L·Λ. subproblems.title: Translates of a test function supported in B_s(0) by centres in the closed ball B̄_R(0) are test functions in B_{2R}(0) with the same integral
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, R, s ∈ ℝ with s < R, φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n with Lebesgue measure) smooth (ContDiff ℝ ⊤) with tsupport φ ⊆ B_s(0) (open ball), and x ∈ closedBall(0, R). Let b(y) := φ(x − y). Then b is smooth (ContDiff ℝ ⊤), b has compact support, tsupport b ⊆ B_{2R}(0), and ∫_{ℝⁿ} φ(x − y) dy = ∫_{ℝⁿ} φ(y) dy.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (R s : ℝ) (φ : Euclid n → ℝ) (x : Euclid n), s < R → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ → tsupport φ ⊆ ball 0 s → x ∈ closedBall 0 R → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (fun y => φ (x - y)) ∧ HasCompactSupport (fun y => φ (x - y)) ∧ tsupport (fun y => φ (x - y)) ⊆ ball 0 (2 * R) ∧ ∫ y, φ (x - y) = ∫ y, φ y
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the selected theorem's supplied proof (b_x = φ(x − ·) is an admissible test function in B_{2R}(0) with ∫b_x = ∫φ), together with the compact-support part of its step 1. Notation: ℝⁿ = Euclid n with Lebesgue measure (volume); e(y) := x − y; b := φ ∘ e, i.e. b(y) = φ(x − y).
1. (φ has compact support.) tsupport φ is closed (isClosed_tsupport) and tsupport φ ⊆ ball(0, s) ⊆ closedBall(0, s) (ball_subset_closedBall). closedBall(0, s) is compact because ℝⁿ is a proper space (isCompact_closedBall). A closed subset of a compact set is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset), so tsupport φ is compact, i.e. HasCompactSupport φ.
2. (e is a smooth homeomorphism.) e(y) = x − y is a homeomorphism of ℝⁿ (it is its own inverse; in Mathlib it is Homeomorph.subLeft x, and (fun y => φ (x − y)) = φ ∘ Homeomorph.subLeft x holds by rfl). It is C^∞, being the difference of the constant map y ↦ x and the identity (contDiff_const.sub contDiff_id).
3. (b is smooth.) b = φ ∘ e is a composition of C^∞ maps, hence ContDiff ℝ ⊤ (ContDiff.comp: hφ.comp (contDiff_const.sub contDiff_id)).
4. (b has compact support.) Precomposition with a homeomorphism preserves compact support: from step 1 and HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph we get HasCompactSupport (φ ∘ e). (Concretely, tsupport(φ ∘ e) = e⁻¹(tsupport φ) = e(tsupport φ) because e = e⁻¹; this is a continuous image of a compact set.)
5. (Support inclusion.) For a homeomorphism e, tsupport(φ ∘ e) = e⁻¹(tsupport φ) (tsupport_comp_eq_preimage). Let y ∈ tsupport b. Then x − y = e(y) ∈ tsupport φ ⊆ ball(0, s), so ‖x − y‖ < s (mem_ball_zero_iff); and x ∈ closedBall(0, R) means ‖x‖ ≤ R (mem_closedBall_zero_iff). Since y = x − (x − y), the triangle inequality (norm_sub_le) gives ‖y‖ ≤ ‖x‖ + ‖x − y‖ < R + s < R + R = 2R, using s < R. Hence y ∈ ball(0, 2R), so tsupport b ⊆ ball(0, 2R).
6. (Integral.) Lebesgue measure on Euclid n is an additive Haar measure, invariant under translations and under negation y ↦ −y. Hence the change of variables y ↦ x − y preserves it and ∫ φ(x − y) dy = ∫ φ(y) dy (integral_sub_left_eq_self φ volume x). This identity is a change of variables by a measure-preserving equivalence and needs no integrability hypothesis.
7. Steps 3, 4, 5 and 6 are exactly the four conjuncts of the conclusion. (No positivity of s or R is used: if s ≤ 0 then ball(0, s) = ∅, φ vanishes identically, and the same argument applies verbatim.) ∎
proof_key_steps: tsupport φ is a closed subset of the compact closedBall(0, s), so φ has compact support.
b = φ ∘ e with e(y) = x − y a smooth self-inverse homeomorphism (Homeomorph.subLeft x), so b is C^∞ and has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph).
tsupport b = e⁻¹(tsupport φ); for such y, ‖y‖ ≤ ‖x‖ + ‖x − y‖ < R + s < 2R, so tsupport b ⊆ ball(0, 2R).
∫ φ(x − y) dy = ∫ φ by invariance of Lebesgue (additive Haar) measure under y ↦ x − y (integral_sub_left_eq_self).

subproblems.title: Mollification of an integrable function by a smooth compactly supported kernel is Lipschitz with constant proportional to its L¹ norm
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n with Lebesgue measure) be smooth (ContDiff ℝ ⊤) with compact support. Then there is a constant L ≥ 0 such that for every set S ⊆ ℝⁿ, every v : ℝⁿ → ℝ Lebesgue integrable on S, and all x, x' ∈ ℝⁿ: |∫_S v(y)φ(x − y) dy − ∫_S v(y)φ(x' − y) dy| ≤ L·(∫_S |v(y)| dy)·dist(x, x').
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (φ : Euclid n → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ → HasCompactSupport φ → ∃ L : ℝ, 0 ≤ L ∧ ∀ (S : Set (Euclid n)) (v : Euclid n → ℝ), IntegrableOn v S → ∀ x x' : Euclid n, |(∫ y in S, v y * φ (x - y)) - ∫ y in S, v y * φ (x' - y)| ≤ L * (∫ y in S, |v y|) * dist x x'
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 3 (regularity of φ; equi-Lipschitz estimate) of the selected theorem's supplied proof, stated for an arbitrary set S and an arbitrary integrable v (the parent uses S = B_{2R}(0), v = u_k). All integrals are with respect to Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝⁿ = Euclid n; ∫_S denotes the integral for volume restricted to S (S need not be measurable).
1. (φ is Lipschitz.) φ is C^∞, hence C¹ (the smoothness order ⊤ is ≠ 0), and has compact support, so φ is globally Lipschitz. There is C ∈ ℝ≥0 with |φ(z) − φ(z')| = dist(φ(z), φ(z')) ≤ C·dist(z, z') for all z, z' ∈ ℝⁿ (ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport with the side condition ⊤ ≠ 0 closed by simp, then LipschitzWith.dist_le_mul and Real.dist_eq). Set L := C (as a real number); then L ≥ 0. L is chosen here, before S, v, x, x', so it depends only on φ.
2. (φ is bounded.) φ is continuous (ContDiff.continuous) with compact support, so there is M ∈ ℝ with |φ(z)| ≤ M for all z (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support).
3. (Integrability.) Fix S, v integrable on S, and x, x' ∈ ℝⁿ. For any z ∈ ℝⁿ, the map y ↦ φ(z − y) is continuous (φ composed with the continuous map y ↦ z − y). Hence it is AE-strongly measurable for volume restricted to S, and it is bounded by M everywhere. Therefore y ↦ v(y)·φ(z − y) is integrable on S (Integrable.mul_bdd: integrable times bounded AE-strongly measurable). Apply this with z = x and with z = x'.
4. (Linearity.) By step 3 and integral_sub, ∫_S v(y)φ(x − y) dy − ∫_S v(y)φ(x' − y) dy = ∫_S g(y) dy, where g(y) := v(y)φ(x − y) − v(y)φ(x' − y).
5. (Pointwise bound.) For every y, g(y) = v(y)·(φ(x − y) − φ(x' − y)) (mul_sub), so |g(y)| = |v(y)|·|φ(x − y) − φ(x' − y)| (abs_mul). By step 1 and translation invariance of the distance, dist(x − y, x' − y) = dist(x, x') (dist_sub_right). So |φ(x − y) − φ(x' − y)| ≤ C·dist(x, x'), and since |v(y)| ≥ 0, |g(y)| ≤ |v(y)|·(C·dist(x, x')).
6. (Integral bound.) First, |∫_S g| ≤ ∫_S |g| (abs_integral_le_integral_abs). The function y ↦ |v(y)|·(C·dist(x, x')) is integrable on S (|v| is integrable on S by Integrable.abs; multiply by a constant with Integrable.mul_const), and |g| ≥ 0 everywhere. So integral_mono_of_nonneg together with step 5 gives ∫_S |g| ≤ ∫_S |v(y)|·(C·dist(x, x')) dy = (∫_S |v|)·C·dist(x, x') (integral_mul_const).
7. (Conclusion.) By steps 4 and 6, |∫_S v(y)φ(x − y) dy − ∫_S v(y)φ(x' − y) dy| ≤ C·(∫_S |v|)·dist(x, x') = L·(∫_S |v|)·dist(x, x'), with L = C ≥ 0 independent of S, v, x, x'. ∎
proof_key_steps: φ is Lipschitz with some constant C ≥ 0 (C¹ with compact support) and bounded by some M (continuous with compact support); take L := C.
For every z, y ↦ v(y)φ(z − y) is integrable on S (integrable times bounded continuous; Integrable.mul_bdd).
The difference of the two integrals equals ∫_S v(y)(φ(x − y) − φ(x' − y)) dy (integral_sub).
Pointwise |v(y)||φ(x − y) − φ(x' − y)| ≤ |v(y)|·C·dist(x, x') by the Lipschitz bound and dist(x − y, x' − y) = dist(x, x').
|∫ g| ≤ ∫|g| ≤ ∫_S |v|·C·dist(x, x') = C(∫_S|v|)dist(x, x') (abs_integral_le_integral_abs, integral_mono_of_nonneg, integral_mul_const).

subproblems.title: Pointwise convergence plus an eventual uniform Lipschitz bound on a compact set gives uniform convergence
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, K ⊆ ℝⁿ (= Euclid n) compact, F_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) arbitrary functions, and a, L ∈ ℝ. Assume (i) F_k(x) → a as k → ∞ for every x ∈ K, and (ii) for all sufficiently large k, |F_k(x) − F_k(x')| ≤ L·dist(x, x') for all x, x' ∈ K. Then F_k converges to the constant function a uniformly on K.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (K : Set (Euclid n)) (F : ℕ → Euclid n → ℝ) (a L : ℝ), IsCompact K → (∀ x ∈ K, Tendsto (fun k => F k x) atTop (𝓝 a)) → (∀ᶠ k in atTop, ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ x' ∈ K, |F k x - F k x'| ≤ L * dist x x') → TendstoUniformlyOn F (fun _ => a) atTop K
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 (uniformity) of the selected theorem's supplied proof, abstracted from w_k to an arbitrary sequence F_k with a constant pointwise limit a. This is the standard ε/3 argument: pointwise convergence plus equicontinuity on a compact set gives uniform convergence.
1. (Reduction to an ε-statement.) By Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff, TendstoUniformlyOn F (fun _ => a) atTop K holds iff for every ε > 0, for all sufficiently large k, dist(a, F_k(x)) < ε for every x ∈ K. On ℝ, dist(p, q) = |p − q| (Real.dist_eq). So fix ε > 0; we must show ∀ᶠ k in atTop, ∀ x ∈ K, |a − F_k(x)| < ε.
2. (Choice of the mesh.) Put L⁺ := max(L, 0), so L⁺ ≥ 0 and L ≤ L⁺, and put η := ε/(3(L⁺ + 1)). Then η > 0, and L⁺·η = (ε/3)·L⁺/(L⁺ + 1) < ε/3 because 0 ≤ L⁺ < L⁺ + 1 and ε > 0 (cross-multiplied: 3·L⁺·ε < 3·(L⁺ + 1)·ε).
3. (Finite η-net.) K is compact, so finite_cover_balls_of_compact (alias IsCompact.finite_cover_balls) with radius η > 0 gives a finite set t ⊆ K with K ⊆ ⋃_{z ∈ t} ball(z, η).
4. (Pointwise convergence on the net.) For each z ∈ t we have z ∈ K, so by (i) F_k(z) → a. By Metric.tendsto_nhds with ε/3 > 0, eventually dist(F_k(z), a) = |F_k(z) − a| < ε/3. Because t is finite, these finitely many eventual statements hold simultaneously (Set.Finite.eventually_all, i.e. Filter.eventually_all_finite): ∀ᶠ k in atTop, ∀ z ∈ t, |F_k(z) − a| < ε/3.
5. (Intersect with the Lipschitz hypothesis.) Hypothesis (ii) is also an eventual statement in k, and two eventual statements hold together eventually (filter_upwards). Fix any k for which both the conclusion of step 4 and the inequality of (ii) hold, and fix x ∈ K.
6. (Nearby centre.) By step 3, x ∈ ball(z, η) for some z ∈ t, i.e. dist(x, z) < η, hence dist(z, x) < η (dist_comm). Since z ∈ t ⊆ K and x ∈ K, (ii) gives |F_k(z) − F_k(x)| ≤ L·dist(z, x) ≤ L⁺·dist(z, x) ≤ L⁺·η < ε/3. The second inequality uses dist(z, x) ≥ 0 and L ≤ L⁺; the third uses L⁺ ≥ 0 and dist(z, x) < η; the last is step 2.
7. (Triangle inequality.) |a − F_k(x)| = |(a − F_k(z)) + (F_k(z) − F_k(x))| ≤ |a − F_k(z)| + |F_k(z) − F_k(x)| = |F_k(z) − a| + |F_k(z) − F_k(x)| < ε/3 + ε/3 < ε, by step 4 (z ∈ t) and step 6.
8. (Conclusion.) Steps 5–7 show ∀ᶠ k in atTop, ∀ x ∈ K, dist(a, F_k(x)) < ε. Since ε > 0 was arbitrary, step 1 gives TendstoUniformlyOn F (fun _ => a) atTop K. If K = ∅, the conclusion of step 5 holds vacuously, so no case split is needed. ∎
Formalization note (optional alternative with the same mathematics): instead of the global net one may use tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_iff_tendstoUniformlyOn_of_compact (K compact) together with Metric.tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_iff. For x ∈ K take the neighbourhood K ∩ ball(x, η) ∈ 𝓝[K] x, and apply the estimate of steps 6–7 with the centre z := x.
proof_key_steps: Reduce to: for every ε > 0, eventually ∀ x ∈ K, |a − F_k(x)| < ε (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff).
Choose η = ε/(3(max(L,0)+1)), so max(L,0)·η < ε/3.
Cover the compact K by finitely many η-balls with centres in a finite t ⊆ K (finite_cover_balls_of_compact).
Eventually every centre z ∈ t satisfies |F_k(z) − a| < ε/3 (finitely many eventualities), and eventually the Lipschitz bound (ii) holds.
For x ∈ K pick z ∈ t with dist(z, x) < η; then |F_k(z) − F_k(x)| < ε/3 and the triangle inequality gives |a − F_k(x)| < ε.
